about: A switch may declare a plus spelling as its negation (`negate="+x"`) and a flag may be spelled with `+` (`flag "+o <option>"`), as the shells' `set +x` and `+o pipefail` are. Plus letters bundle as dash letters do.

vectors.doc: `+x` is the negated spelling a switch declares with `negate="+x"`.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: `-x +x` leaves the switch off, and `+x -x` on.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: `+eux` negates each letter in turn, as `-eux` sets them.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A value-taking flag spelled with `+` takes the following word: `+o pipefail`.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A value-taking letter ends a plus bundle, as it ends a dash bundle.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A plus token containing a letter nothing declares is not a bundle, and becomes a word.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: Under `unknown_flags "error"` an unrecognized plus token in a command with plus spellings is refused.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "error"
flag "-x" negate="+x"

vectors.doc: A command that declares no plus spelling reads `+x` as an ordinary word.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "error"
flag "-x"
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: After `--` a plus token is a value.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A plus token the command reads as flags stops a flag wanting a value, as a dash flag does.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A plus spelling the default subcommand declares routes there, as a dash one does.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
default_subcommand "run"
cmd "run" {
    flag "-x" negate="+x"
    arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: No plus spelling is in scope at the root, so the token is an ordinary word there.
A `+` word that names no plus spelling still reaches a positional that claims the sigil.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
arg "[tag]" sigil="+"

vectors.doc: A flag is read before a positional, whichever sigil the positional claims.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
arg "[tag]" sigil="+"

vectors.doc: A lone `+` names no letter, so it is a word.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A value-taking plus letter takes the rest of the token, as a short does.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: `=` separates a plus spelling from its value, as it does a short's.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: Once a letter takes a value the bundle is over, so the remaining letters are that value.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A bundle is all-or-nothing, as a dash bundle is: one unknown letter makes the token a word.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "value"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: `+x` is not tied to `-x`: a flag may be spelled with `+` alone.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-x"
flag "trace-off: +x"
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A plus spelling binds where it is written, before the subcommand it precedes.
A global plus spelling binds after the subcommand too.
Everything past an external subcommand's name belongs to it, plus words included.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
external_subcommand #true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A plus spelling that takes a value needs one, as a short does.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A `+` word that names no spelling is an ordinary value, so a flag still takes it.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "-e" negate="+e"
flag "-u" negate="+u"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
flag "-o <option>" var=#true
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" var=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: A variadic flag stops at a plus bundle and lets it bind.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--include <pat>..."
flag "-e" negate="+e"
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: An unrecognized `+` word is a value, so the run keeps it.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "--include <pat>..."
flag "-e" negate="+e"
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: `+o=pipefail` binds attached, which `require_equals` accepts and a detached value would not.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "unset-option: +o <option>" require_equals=#true
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: An attached value stays one: `+o=--force` is a value, not the `--force` flag.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "unset-option: +o <option>"
flag "--force"
arg "[args]..."

vectors.doc: `+opipefail` carries its value, so the word after it can still name a subcommand.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "unset-option: +o <option>"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
cmd "run" {
    arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: `+xo` leaves `+o` wanting a value, which the following word supplies even where a subcommand has that name.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
flag "unset-option: +o <option>"
flag "-x" negate="+x"
cmd "run" {
    arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: `+o` belongs to the default subcommand, so the route is taken even though the parent has a plus spelling of its own.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "error"
default_subcommand "run"
default_subcommand_flags #true
flag "-e" negate="+e"
cmd "run" {
    flag "unset-option: +o <option>"
    arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: The same for a switch's negated spelling.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "error"
default_subcommand "run"
default_subcommand_flags #true
flag "-e" negate="+e"
cmd "run" {
    flag "-x" negate="+x"
    arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: The parent declares no plus spelling at all, and the route is still taken.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "error"
default_subcommand "run"
default_subcommand_flags #true
cmd "run" {
    flag "unset-option: +o <option>"
    arg "[args]..."
}

vectors.doc: A parent spelling binds on the parent, and a default-only one still routes after it.
vectors.spec:
name "ex"
bin "ex"
unknown_flags "error"
default_subcommand "run"
default_subcommand_flags #true
flag "-e" negate="+e"
cmd "run" {
    flag "-x" negate="+x"
    arg "[args]..."
}
